person: Walt Brenner is 66 and owns a 24-person surveying and renovation firm, where he does his own HR. The firm runs its own health plan, and a part-time bookkeeper helps with payroll. This quarter he has a layoff, a quit, a divorce and a daughter aging off the plan, and he has been told letters must go out on a deadline. He has heard 'a quit gets no COBRA' from his broker and does not know whether that is right. He prints everything, distrusts anything that looks like a sales pitch, and wants to be told plainly which letters go out, by when, and what it costs him if one is missed.
stated_up_front: I am not a computer person. I have a couple of people who left or lost their insurance this quarter and somebody told me there's a letter I have to mail them on a deadline. Figure out who gets one and tell me plain what it costs me if I skip it.

facts.truth: Surveyor Dale Ostrowski was laid off September 4; his coverage on the Blue Cross portal ended September 30.
Office hand Tamika Reese quit October 2; her coverage runs through October 31. His broker says a quit gets no COBRA.
Foreman Ray Pruitt's letter about his divorce reached Walt's office October 14, and the divorce was final in late September. His wife Carol is on the plan.
The carrier shows Carol at a separate rental on Alder Street, not Ray's address, because they separated last spring.
Estimator Gil Navarro wrote a letter that arrived October 12 saying his daughter Marisol turned 26 on October 9; she is on his plan.

facts.about: A laid-off worker who was never enrolled
facts.truth: Seasonal laborer Eddie Cass was let go September 18; he turned down the health plan when hired and was never enrolled.
Crew hand Luis Varga was cut to 32 hours a week in September and is still on the plan.
Roofer Hank Dwyer was laid off in July, and an election notice went to him on August 12 on the plan's letterhead.
An email from a company called BenefitBridge offers to send all the COBRA notices for $85 a month per person; he has not answered it.
The plan's COBRA rules are in the three-ring binder with the carrier contract, and he has the payroll stubs for the firm's numbers.

unknowns: Whether the plan counts its deadline from the day coverage ended or from the day the employee's letter arrived.
Whether someone who quits is owed a COBRA notice (his broker says no; he can't tell if that is right).
How many days after a divorce an employee can report it before the plan no longer has to send a notice.
Whether Carol Pruitt needs her own notice mailed to her separate address.
